About

Our Story

A ministry of Ravenswood Baptist Church, serving families on the north side of Chicago since 1972.

Committed to Chicago's children

Ravenswood Christian School exists to come alongside parents to help train their children.

We are committed to offering a quality academic education with a Christian perspective to the children of Chicago. We help parents teach and train their young people to achieve academic excellence while using a Bible-based curriculum.

We have been providing a Christian education in this city for more than fifty years. We do that by teaching the core subjects well, so that students are prepared for the work God has for them. We do not stop there. We also teach a Christian worldview through solid Bible instruction integrated across every subject, which builds the foundation of values and ethics students need to be not only successful but good neighbors.

We accomplish this in a safe environment, with teachers who have a passion for instructing and discipling young people in God's truth.

Ravenswood first met in the basement of Ravenswood Baptist Church in 1972. It took several years to build the school's own building, which turns fifty years old this year.

Confirmed with Duston: the founding year (1972) and the "over fifty years" language are both correct and now standardized across the site. The added detail above, that the school started in the church basement before its own building was constructed, came directly from this conversation.

Our Mission

By God's grace, we are committed to:

Christlike character

Building Christlike character in our students, in the classroom and in how they treat one another.

A safe place to learn

Providing a secure, well-supervised environment where children are free to grow.

The individual student

Focusing on individual student development rather than moving a crowd through a curriculum.

Academic excellence

Achieving academic excellence through researched, proven teaching methods.

Readiness

Preparing students to meet the challenges of today with wisdom and conviction.

Our Deep Hope

That our students would behold the beauty of God, believe the power of the Gospel, and become Christlike as they engage God's world with love and wisdom.

Decision from our meeting: the Deep Hope is the primary statement and leads the site. The mission statement above is kept and clearly labeled as the mission so the two are never confused. Behold / Believe / Become is used as the storyline in smaller spaces, not on the same page as the Deep Hope. Confirm approach
How a Ravenswood education is different

Freedom to grow in faith

Students thrive in a Christ-centered environment where they are free to openly express their faith and are continually encouraged to deepen their relationship with God.

Teachers who invest

Our teachers do more than teach. They care about each student's spiritual growth, social development, and academic success.

A lower ratio

Ravenswood offers a lower teacher-to-student ratio than most Chicago public schools, which lets teachers give students the personalized attention that builds real confidence.

About

What We Believe

A Bible-believing school, concentrated on developing both the intellectual knowledge and the faith foundation of every student.

Our theology and doctrine is in line with orthodox Christianity as found in most Bible-believing churches.

  • We believe in the verbal inspiration, preservation, and authority of the Scriptures.
  • We believe the Bible to be the inspired, the only infallible, authoritative Word of God.
  • We believe that the Bible reveals God, the fall of man, the way of salvation, and God's plan and purpose for the ages.
  • We believe in God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit.
  • We believe in the deity, virgin birth, sacrificial death, and bodily resurrection of Jesus Christ.
  • We believe that salvation is by grace plus nothing and minus nothing. The conditions of salvation are repentance and faith.
  • We believe that men are justified by faith alone and are accounted righteous before God only through the merit of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
  • We believe in the imminent return of Jesus Christ.
Do we have to be a Christian family to enroll? We are upfront with every family that although we welcome students of all faiths, your child will be taught from the Bible as part of daily instruction.

Ravenswood Baptist Church

Ravenswood Christian School is a ministry of Ravenswood Baptist Church.

One family, one mission

The school shares a campus, a leadership, and a purpose with Ravenswood Baptist Church. Pastor Duston Moore serves as both Lead Pastor and Head of School. The generosity of church members is part of what keeps tuition well below the actual cost of educating a student here.

Academics

Academics

A Christ-centered, academically rigorous education built on the Abeka curriculum and shaped by the Teaching for Transformation framework.

Learning with Christ at the center

The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge. (Proverbs 1:7)

Our curriculum is built on the teaching of God's Word, keeping Christ at the center of everything we do. We partner with families to prepare students for a life of purpose, using the trusted Abeka curriculum alongside methods that build deep understanding rather than short-term recall.

A strong foundation, revisited

Students build on a strong foundation as they progress through the grades, returning to key concepts to deepen their understanding. This spiral approach reinforces early lessons and prevents learning gaps.

Every kind of learner

Every child learns differently, so we build auditory, visual, and hands-on activities into each lesson. Addressing all learning preferences teaches adaptability along with the material itself.

Connected across subjects

Learning does not happen in isolation here. Students might study a historical figure in history, meet them again in literature, build a project around them, and apply artistic skills to it, all reinforcing one understanding of the world.

Academics

How We Teach

Ravenswood Christian School is a Teaching for Transformation school.

This page is the single most important piece of content still outstanding. The structure below is built and ready. It needs the real language from Duston and Mindy: a short description of Teaching for Transformation in Duston's own words, why the school uses it, and which through lines Ravenswood is keeping and in what wording. Everything on this page is currently Enduo's placeholder framing. Duston · TFT description Mindy · through lines

What it is

Teaching for Transformation is a pedagogy, not a curriculum. It changes how a lesson is built, so that a math class or a history class is not just a Christian school's version of a public school class.

Students are taught to see God's story at work in the subject in front of them, and then to live that story out in real work with real people. That is why our field trips are called field work, and why students spend time in the museums, neighborhoods, and organizations of this city rather than only reading about them.

Our Deep Hope is that our students would behold the beauty of God, believe the power of the Gospel, and become Christlike as they engage God's world with love and wisdom.

Our Through Lines

Through lines are the habits and postures we want to form in every student, in every subject, across every year they are here.

Field Work

At Ravenswood, learning extends beyond the classroom into one of the most dynamic cities in the world. Within a few miles of our school, students have access to world-class museums, research institutions, cultural communities, public leaders, artists, entrepreneurs, and nonprofits working to solve real problems.

Students study history, science, culture, and economics not only in textbooks but in the places where those stories are unfolding. Over time they begin to understand something essential: learning is connected to real people with real needs.

Field Work This Year

Each grade takes its learning out into the city. Here is where our students are headed in the 2026 to 2027 school year.

Pre-K

Caring for Backyard Birds. Students meet a bird care expert and build a backyard birdfeeder.

5th & 6th Grade

Ancient Greek History. A visit to the National Hellenic Museum.

7th & 8th Grade

First Aid. A day at the Museum of Science and Industry.

9th & 10th Grade

Research and Radon. A seminar at Harold Washington.

11th Grade

Honoring Stories and Voices. A visit to the Holocaust Museum, with students creating a final Honor Stories project.

12th Grade

Spanish Culture. A visit to the Spanish Heritage Museum.

Academics

Preschool & Kindergarten

Play-based learning with real academic foundations, in classes small enough that every child is known.

A day built for three, four, and five year olds

We believe play is essential to a child's development, so we combine Abeka with a play-based curriculum. Children work on letter sounds, writing skills, counting and number sense, 2D and 3D shapes, colors, character formation, social and emotional regulation, STEM activities, large and small motor skills, music, and Bible verse and poetry memorization.

Class sizes are small, with a 1:10 teacher-to-child ratio.

Hours and scheduling

  • Open 7:30am to 5:00pm daily
  • Half days run 7:30am to 12:00pm
  • Choose 3 half or full days, and pick which three days work for your family
  • Or choose 5 half or full days
  • Morning care from 7:30am and after care until 5:00pm are included in tuition at no extra charge
  • We accept new students who are fully potty trained through December

Preschool Questions

Does my child have to be fully potty trained?

Yes. We understand that small children will have occasional accidents, but children should be able to tell when they need to go to the bathroom and communicate that to the teacher.

Does my child have to take a nap?

Each child will have a rest time. If they are not tired they do not need to fall asleep, but they must be able to lie quietly so others can rest.

Does the class have a set three day schedule?

No. Anyone who enrolls their child for three days can choose which three days work best for their family's current needs.

Can I drop off and pick up my child at any time of day?

We ask that all children are dropped off no later than 9:00am. If you need a later drop off, please communicate that with the teacher. Children should be picked up between 3:00 and 3:15pm unless the child has a doctor's appointment.

What curriculum do you use?

Because we believe play is essential to a child's development, we use a combination of Abeka and a play-based curriculum to enhance the preschool learning environment.

Do you accept new students throughout the year?

We accept any child who is age eligible and fully potty trained before December 31 of the current school year. Confirm age cutoff wording

Curriculum

Elementary school at Ravenswood Christian School is made up of 1st through 4th graders. Our students are nurtured and taught in the Abeka curriculum along with a Teaching for Transformation framework.

This framework, along with our biblically based curriculum, shapes a Christ-centered worldview that equips students to understand their value and purpose as they develop an understanding of the world around them. Our small class sizes allow teachers to guide students in hands-on instruction. Students are invited to see God's story and live God's story in our daily lessons and activities.

Structure

  • Multi-period schedule
  • Small class sizes
  • Academic rigor and support
  • Field work built in
  • Co-curricular electives in Spanish and Music

Elementary Questions

What are the school start and end times?

Classes start promptly at 8:15am for all elementary students. School is dismissed at 3:15pm.

How do morning drop-offs and afternoon pick-ups work?

Morning care starts at 7:30am and runs until 7:55am. School is dismissed at 3:15pm. Students who are not picked up at that time are signed in to after care, which begins at 3:30pm and runs until 5:00pm.

What if my child needs to be picked up early for an appointment?

Parents sign out their student at the main office. Office personnel will notify the teacher to dismiss the student.

What do I do if my child is sick?

If your child is running a fever or vomiting, he or she must stay home. Please call the school office to report the absence before the school day begins. For further information, see the RCS handbook.

How does school lunch work?

Elementary lunch starts at 11:30am. Parents may send microwaveable lunches with their students as well as snacks. We are not a nut-free school, but we take allergies seriously. Teachers notify the parents in their class about food allergies.

Middle & High School Questions

What is the average class size and student-teacher ratio?

Our student-teacher ratio is 6:1.

How do you support students with varying learning paces?

Grade-level concepts are taught, but differentiation is built into the instruction.

How does the school communicate with parents?

School communication is handled through weekly newsletters and text updates.

How long is the school day?

Seven hours. Students must be in homeroom by 8:15am and are dismissed by 3:15pm.

Are meals and snacks provided?

No, but students are encouraged to bring snacks to eat during their breaks, and microwaves are available for warming lunches. We also have Pizza Days where students can bring money to purchase pizza. We are not a nut-free school, but we take allergies seriously.

What does the school day schedule look like?

Students receive a copy of the schedule that outlines their class rotation between teachers for corresponding subjects.

What competitive athletics are offered, and at what grade do they begin?

Cross country is offered for 3rd through 12th graders.

Is there a uniform or dress code?

We have a standard of appearance outlined in our handbook.

What curriculum do you use?

We primarily use Abeka, supplemented with Summit Ministries for Bible, novel units for literature, and various sources for history.

How do you support students who are academically advanced?

We offer a range of electives as well as dual enrollment options for 11th and 12th graders that they can take in addition to their required courses.

What is the school's view on homework?

Students often need extra practice with new concepts, skills, or facts. After reasonable in-class time is spent on the material, the teacher may assign homework for the practice needed to reach mastery. The amount varies by grade and is outlined in our handbook.

How does the school respond to a student not meeting academic standards?

The school addresses academic progress directly with the family and discusses findings and alternatives.

One item pulled for review: the source document includes a student body diversity breakdown by percentage. Enduo recommends discussing whether to publish exact percentages or describe the diversity of the school in plain language instead, since figures like these change every year and require annual updating. Tuition Assistance

Cost should not be the reason a child misses a Christ-centered education.

How it works

Ravenswood Christian School partners with Christian families to provide a Christ-centered education. Tuition assistance is intended to help families with demonstrated financial need. Applications are reviewed confidentially by the Head of School, with final approval by the School Board.

Before you apply

  • Eligibility: Kindergarten through 12th grade
  • Complete every section of the application
  • Attach all required documentation
  • Deadline: August 17, 2026 for the 2026-2027 school year
  • Submitting an application does not guarantee assistance

Required documents

  • Federal tax return
  • W-2 forms
  • Two recent pay stubs
  • Extraordinary expense documentation, if applicable
  • Any other supporting documentation, optional

Apply for assistance

The application asks for household and student information, income, monthly expenses, assets, and a short section on why you have chosen a Christian education for your child.

Start the Application

Frequently Asked Questions

The questions our office and tour staff hear most often.

General

What grades does Ravenswood serve?

Preschool for three, four, and five year olds through 12th grade, all on one campus in Lincoln Square.

What are the school day hours?

Students must be in homeroom by 8:15am and are dismissed at 3:15pm. Morning care starts at 7:30am and after care runs until 5:00pm.

Do we have to be a Christian family to enroll?

We are upfront with every family that although we welcome students of all faiths, your child will be taught from the Bible as part of daily instruction. We currently have families of other faith backgrounds enrolled at Ravenswood.

What curriculum do you use?

We primarily use Abeka, supplemented with Summit Ministries for Bible, novel units for literature, and various sources for history. Preschool combines Abeka with a play-based curriculum.

Where is the school located?

4437 N. Seeley Avenue, Chicago, Illinois 60625, on the north side of Chicago in the Lincoln Square neighborhood.

Daily life

How does lunch work?

Students bring their own lunch. Microwaves are available. Elementary lunch begins at 11:30am. Secondary students can also buy pizza on Pizza Days. We are not a nut-free school, but we take allergies seriously and teachers notify families in their class about allergies.

Do you offer before and after care?

Yes. Our Extended Care Program provides before and after school care with indoor and outdoor play, activities, movies, games, and daily homework help, supervised by adults with help from secondary student aides. Hours, cost, ages, late fees, drop-in policy

What is the dress code?

We have a standard of appearance outlined in our handbook, available on the Parent Hub.

How does the school communicate with parents?

Through weekly newsletters and text updates, plus daily teacher communication in the younger grades.

Field work in Chicago

Field Work

At Ravenswood, learning extends beyond the classroom into one of the most dynamic cities in the world. Within a few miles of our school, students have access to world-class museums, research institutions, cultural communities, public leaders, artists, entrepreneurs, and nonprofit organizations working to solve real problems.

Students study history, science, culture, and economics not only in textbooks but in the places where those stories are unfolding. They learn in museums and engage with communities working for change. Over time they begin to understand something essential: learning is connected to real people with real needs.

Before & After Care

Our Extended Care Program was developed to help provide for the needs of our school's working parents. This before and after school program provides quality, convenient, and affordable childcare for school families.

The program includes indoor and outdoor play, activities, movies, games, and daily homework help, with adult supervision at all times and additional assistance from our secondary student aides.

Needed: exact hours, cost, ages served, staffing, pickup procedure, late fees, and whether drop-in is allowed. This is one of the biggest deciding factors for working parents and currently appears nowhere on the site. Office

Safety

Ravenswood Christian School emphasizes maintaining situational awareness, fostering a supportive classroom climate, and executing emergency protocols with calm authority.

  • Controlled building access
  • Security cameras
  • Entrance doors locked
  • Classroom doors locked
  • Check-in at the desk
  • Drills during school
  • Emergency go-kits

Community

Learning flourishes within a community marked by love, respect, service, and accountability. We seek to cultivate relationships that reflect the unity of the body of Christ, encouraging students to honor one another, resolve conflict biblically, and faithfully serve those around them.

At Ravenswood Christian School, students grow within a single, connected community that knows them, challenges them, and walks with them. Families who choose Ravenswood are choosing a formation pathway that disciples students to behold the beauty of God, believe the power of the Gospel, and become Christlike as they engage God's world with love and wisdom.

Physical Education

Ravenswood Christian School is not just a school. For more than fifty years we have partnered with parents to disciple children, nurture faith, and provide strong academics in a safe, loving, Christ-centered community.

But many families who want this kind of education cannot afford tuition, even at our reduced nonprofit rates. That is why we launched the Scholarship Fund, so that cost never stands between a child and a Gospel-centered education.

Your gift

  • Opens doors for children to hear and live the Gospel daily
  • Provides scholarships for families in need
  • Supports small class sizes where every child is known
  • Grows the Ravenswood community and multiplies opportunities for discipleship
